_doc: Shared guard test vectors at the normalized-event level (replayed by tests/test_shoal_guard.py; a
TypeScript port replays the same file).  Placeholders: $HOME (temp home), $WORK ($HOME/work, default cwd),
$TMPDIR ($HOME/tmpdir, exported as TMPDIR), $STATE (state base).  Event defaults: host = vector host
(claude), session_id s1, turn_id t1, cwd $WORK, is_subagent false, role null, tool_name derived from
tool_kind (edit=Edit, dispatch=Agent, background_shell=Bash, shell=Bash, other=Read), paths [], dispatched_role null,
command null (shell events: the Bash command text).  An explicit null
overrides a default.  Env defaults: XDG_STATE_HOME=$HOME/xdg-state, TMPDIR=$TMPDIR; null deletes a key.
Setup: dirs, symlinks {link: target}, chmod, write {file: text}, turn {session, turn_id, role} (classifier
file), turn_legacy_prompt_id, state_file/turn_file {session, content}, log_prefill_bytes.  Checks:
files_exist/files_absent, modes, file_contents, log_contains/log_lacks, log_size_max, log_rotated_bytes (guard.jsonl.1 size), foreign_owner
(paths relative to the guard dir whose owner is simulated as another uid).  The log is always checked
against log_whitelist.
SHOAL_GUARD_SUBAGENT_WRITE (E1, docs/specs/guard-every-gate): e1_*/e2_* vectors; subagent edit/shell events with role = agent type (null = none).
R2 decides `advise` (never deny); R1 decides `advise` on every host except claude, where it decides `deny`
(enforce) or `would_deny` (shadow); G4 (tool_kind background_shell, claude only) decides `deny`/`would_deny`.
G5 (tool_kind shell, claude only): a command that writes a non-exempt file (shell_write_targets) gets R1's decision
while the turn is classified, undispatched and not #direct; otherwise `allow` with rule direct / dispatched /
uncounted (never counted toward R2).  A shell event that writes nothing decides `none` and logs nothing.
expect.notify is true on the first advise of a turn that a claude/codex host in enforce mode prints as
additionalContext, false on later ones and on other hosts/modes.  Prompt events may set direct=true (the
user prompt held a standalone #direct token; default false).  A step may carry write_turn {session,
turn_id, role}: the classifier file is rewritten before that step runs.
SHOAL_GUARD_R1 (docs/specs/guard-declared-direct): env_defaults is merged under every vector's env (null deletes a key).
The v3.1.0 vectors run with SHOAL_GUARD_R1=classified; the declare_*/off_*/r1_* vectors from v3.2.0 set it to null (the host
default: declare on claude, classified elsewhere) or to the value they exercise.  In `declare` mode R1 and G5 decide `deny` /
`would_deny` (rule R1, message DECLARE) unless the turn is direct, dispatched or declared; a shell event whose command is
exactly `: shoal-direct <reason>` (parse_declaration) decides `state` / rule `declare`, logs the reason in the `reason` field

and releases the turn (allow, rule `declared`); a classification file with role parent_local counts as declared. codex has the same rule (tool `Bash` = shell event, `apply_patch` = edit) since 3.2.1; grok, agy and opencode stay classified.

3.3.0: `strict` is the default on claude and codex (SHOAL_GUARD_R1 unset, empty or unrecognized): R1 and G5 deny unless the turn is direct, dispatched or exempt; a declaration is an ordinary no-op (no state, no log) and a classification file has no effect (message STRICT). The declare_* and r1_*_selects_declare vectors select `declare` explicitly; grok, agy and opencode stay classified.

3.3.1 (M11): on claude "a write role was dispatched" unlocks when the role has started: the dispatch call decides allow/dispatch_pending (state pending+1) and a step with event kind subagent_start (role = SubagentStart agent_type, turn_id = its prompt_id, same session) decides state/dispatch_started (pending-1, dispatched) for a write role with a pending dispatch, skip/start_without_pending without one, skip_reason prompt_id_mismatch when its turn_id differs from the guard turn (it still releases), and none for any non-write role. Other hosts unlock at the dispatch call and ignore start events.

3.4.0 (shared-rules B2-B4): a step with event kind stop (turn_id = the Stop payload's prompt_id / turn_id, stop_hook_active = its raw value) decides block / rule STOP when the turn is changed (a non-exempt main edit or shell write was allowed; claude: a write role started, other hosts: a write role dispatched), unchecked (after the latest change a verify-level role was dispatched or started, or main ran a plain foreground shell call that writes nothing and is not a declaration), stop_hook_active is exactly false, the mode is enforce, SHOAL_GUARD_STOP is not off and this turn has not been blocked yet; would_block (nothing persisted) in shadow; none in every other case, skip for missing/invalid ids and a non-boolean stop_hook_active. Only claude and codex ever block; grok, agy and opencode decide none. The block message is MESSAGES.STOP (en / zh-TW).

3.x (guard-every-gate S2, codex): codex joins START_UNLOCK_HOSTS and the E1 default-on hosts. A subagent_start step carries agent_id (the new agent) and turn_id null (its own turn is not main's); a write role releases one pending dispatch once per agent_id (skip_reason agent_already_started on a repeat, missing_id without an agent_id), and a tool step with is_subagent, a write-level role and an agent_id releases one pending dispatch when no start event came (the hook is not approved yet). #direct: a subagent_start while main's turn carried #direct records the agent_id (state direct_agents, last 32) and E1 for that agent_id decides none; unreadable state, another session or another agent decides E1.

3.x (guard-every-gate S4, grok): grok joins the enforce-default, DECLARE_HOSTS (strict by default), START_UNLOCK_HOSTS and E1 default-on hosts. A subagent_start step carries agent_id (the subagent id) and records subagent id -> {session, role, direct} in state/grok.agents.json (the last 64) whatever its role; a tool step whose session_id is a recorded id is a subagent call of the recorded role (is_subagent is filled in, a missing role comes from the record), and its E1 `#direct` release is the recorded flag (main's turn carried #direct at the start). A subagent step with no record keeps the role rules and is never released by #direct; an unreadable record means no record. The stop step on grok logs would_block (rule STOP) and never blocks unless SHOAL_GUARD_STOP is enforce (then block once per turn); off silences it.

agy (docs/specs/guard-every-gate S5): extra event keys `workspace` (session_start, dispatch), `dispatched_roles` (dispatch), `fully_idle` (stop). Main vs subagent is not in the event: it is inferred from session_start / dispatch order, so those vectors drive it with those events and a distinct session_id per conversation.

3.6.0 (guard-every-gate E8): a step with event kind post_shell (tool_kind shell, command, turn_id; is_subagent for a subagent) is the PostToolUse of a shell call that really ran, on claude and codex only; it decides none. A plain foreground one after a change sets checked and records post_seen; until the session's first post_shell, a PreToolUse shell call still sets checked (fallback for a registration without PostToolUse); afterwards PreToolUse no longer counts. Other hosts ignore post_shell and keep the PreToolUse rule. The post_* vectors cover both.

Guard chain (docs/specs/modular-install S2): the chain vectors set SHOAL_GUARD_CHAIN_FILE=$HOME/chain.json (the manifest's `chain` array; XDG_DATA_HOME/shoal/modules.json when unset) and SHOAL_GUARD_CHAIN_TIMEOUT_MS, and write the manifest through setup.write. Members are `python3 $REPO/tests/fixtures/chain/member.py <mode>` ($REPO = repository root; PATH comes from the test process). A step event may carry raw_payload (the exact stdin bytes handed to members; default: the event as JSON). A member deny becomes decision deny (tool), block (stop) or, in shadow, would_deny / would_block, rule chain, reason `<name>: <reason>`; a member error or timeout allows and logs chain_error / chain_timeout (log fields member, ms). TypeScript replays them through applyChain after evaluate.

Guard chain member interface (issue miyago9267/shoal#3, 3.8.0): a manifest entry's `events` (default ["PreToolUse"]; PreToolUse, PostToolUse, UserPromptSubmit, SessionEnd, Stop) picks which events reach the member, by the event's canonical name (kind tool=PreToolUse, post_shell and post_tool=PostToolUse, prompt=UserPromptSubmit, session_end=SessionEnd, stop=Stop). Event kinds post_tool (a PostToolUse of an edit tool; tool_name) and session_end carry no rule and only reach the chain. Only a PreToolUse (or Stop) deny blocks; a deny elsewhere is logged only. A member's `context` string lands in the step result as `context` (several joined by a newline; none when a member denies) and is logged as chain_context without its text; `member`/`version` are logged as chain_report (reason `id=<member> version=<version>`). Members see SHOAL_GUARD_HOST and SHOAL_GUARD_EVENT in their env. SHOAL_GUARD_CHAIN_BUDGET_MS shortens the whole chain's time; a member that finds it used up is skipped with chain_budget. A manifest record for the host without dispatch-guard WITH chain members for the host is chain-only: dispatch rules off, chain on, in the host's own mode; without members it is mode off as before. Converting `context` into the host's output (Claude additionalContext) is the CLI layer, covered by tests/test_shoal_guard.py.
_lane_doc: Dispatch lanes (SHOAL_GUARD_LANES, default on): a main dispatch of a write role (applier, executor, sol-executor, security-executor) must carry dispatch_desc starting with [fast] (applier) / [complex] (executor, sol-executor) / [rigorous] (security-executor); missing or mismatched = deny / rule LANE (would_deny in shadow). agy carries dispatch_descs (one per Subagents[] entry, its Role field). env_defaults turns the rule off for the older vectors; lane_* vectors set it to null (delete = default on).
